subject: Confirming non-learning commitment, retention exceptions, and deletion workflow
messages:
From: Elisa Monroe <elisa.monroe@brightleafhealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@brightleafhealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify: 'we do not train on customer data' + retention edge cases

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this. We’re finalizing our vendor assurance checklist for BrightLeaf’s LLM integrations and need explicit language and operational details around two items before we can complete procurement: 1) the assertion that customer content will not be used to train or improve Redwood’s models, and 2) concrete retention/deletion paths for content after customers request deletion (including backups, debug snapshots, KV caches, and logs).

Specifically:
- Can you confirm in writing that BrightLeaf data will not be included in any training corpora (including research experiments) for any Redwood models?
- If deletion is requested, what is the end-to-end timeline for: active indexes/archives, backups/snapshots, ephemeral caches, and diagnostic logs?
- How do you handle legal holds or e-discovery requests that may supersede normal deletion timelines?

We may ask for an attestation letter for our security team; an appendix that maps retention windows to artifact types would be ideal. Could you also note any differences across your Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options?

Appreciate a short summary and any artifacts you can share (attestation, retention table). We’re aiming to sign the agreement next week.

Best,
Elisa
Senior Procurement Manager
BrightLeaf Health

Attachments: none
From: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elisa Monroe <elisa.monroe@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 19:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify: 'we do not train on customer data' + retention edge cases

Hi Elisa — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: Redwood will not use BrightLeaf customer content to train, fine-tune, or evaluate our models. Below I’ve outlined the operational nuances and attachments that should help your security team.

1) Training/Model Use
- Commitment: Redwood does not and will not include customer-provided inference content from our Hosted API in our model training or any public training corpora. This applies to production input/output text, uploaded files, or transcripts generated as part of inference.
- Research exceptions: internal, synthetic-driven research never ingests raw customer content. Any internal improvements are performed on open-source datasets or synthetic data derived from non-customer sources.
- Deployment differences: Dedicated and Private deployments provide stronger assurance — Dedicated gives dedicated GPU pools and logical separation; Private (VPC or on-prem) keeps data entirely under your control.

2) Retention & Deletion (high level) — see attached Retention_Matrix_Brief.xlsx for a concise mapping:
- Active data (indexes, customer-created objects): deleted within 24–72 hours after a delete API call; tombstone markers may persist 7 days to allow for in-flight request reconciliation.
- Short-term logs/telemetry: aggregated metrics retained 90 days; request-level logs used for troubleshooting kept 30 days by default and purged automatically.
- Backups & snapshots: scheduled snapshots retained up to 90 days for Hosted customers (configurable for Dedicated/Private). For Dedicated customers we can negotiate reduced snapshot retention in contract.
- Debug snapshots / traces: ephemeral debug artifacts are created on-demand and are deleted within 7–30 days; these are flagged as non-production and are excluded from any training pipelines.
- KV caches & prefix caches: designed to be ephemeral; persistent caches are optional and subject to customer control. Default behavior is in-memory or short-lived on-disk caches that expire within 24 hours.

3) Legal holds & e-discovery
- Legal holds: if BrightLeaf issues a legal hold, we preserve the specified artifacts until the hold is released. Holds are handled via our legal intake process; retention windows are suspended while a legally valid hold is active. We provide a point of contact and formal acknowledgement for each hold.

4) Evidence & Attestation
- Attached: Redwood_No-Learning_Attestation_v2.pdf (formal attestation letter) and the Retention_Matrix_Brief.xlsx. We can also provide SOC 2 Type II report under NDA or an auditor redacted summary.

5) Operational controls & encryption
- Data at rest and in transit is encrypted (TLS + AES-256). For Private deployments, keys can be managed via your KMS/HSM.

Next steps: I’ve attached the attestation and a compact retention matrix. If you want, we can set a 30-minute call with Mina (privacy ops) and Grace (product ops) to walk through the matrix and discuss contract language.

Thanks — I’ll follow up to schedule if that works.

—Markus Klein
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555‑0147

Attachments: Redwood_No-Learning_Attestation_v2.pdf, Retention_Matrix_Brief.xlsx
From: Elisa Monroe <elisa.monroe@brightleafhealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@brightleafhealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify: 'we do not train on customer data' + retention edge cases

Markus — thanks for the thorough reply and the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from our security team after a quick pass:

- Backups/snapshots: you noted 90 days for Hosted. If a deletion request comes on day 45, will the backup copy be removed immediately or only when that snapshot expires? We need to understand whether BrightLeaf data could persist in any immutable backup beyond our deletion request.
- Tombstone semantics: can you confirm whether tombstones are searchable or retrievable by any internal tooling during the 7-day reconciliation window?
- Debug snapshots: if an engineer creates a debug snapshot during a support engagement, what is the approval workflow and audit trail for that snapshot?

Also please confirm whether the attestation can be countersigned (we expect to include it as an exhibit to the agreement). Lastly, can you add our procurement contact (legal@brightleafhealth.com) to any attestation delivery so our legal team has the artifact directly.

Elisa

From: mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, legal@brightleafhealth.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify: 'we do not train on customer data' + retention edge cases

Hi Elisa — Mina from Privacy Ops here. Quick clarifications to the three bullets from your security team:

- Backups & snapshots: Hosted snapshots are immutable at the time they are created (point-in-time). If you request deletion and a customer object exists inside an existing snapshot, we do not edit historical snapshots. However: 
  • We offer two mitigations — (1) expiring snapshot retention windows to minimize exposure (we default to 90 days), and (2) for contractual commitments we can implement snapshot scrubbing for specific customers (removing or redacting objects from snapshot archives) as part of an enterprise SLA. That scrubbing process is logged and tracked.
- Tombstones: tombstone markers are internal metadata flags used to prevent resurrecting deleted objects during replication and reconciliation. They are not returned in normal API searches or query results; internal tooling can surface tombstones only to authorized ops staff during recon workflows. Access is audited.
- Debug snapshots: engineers must file a support ticket; debug snapshots require approval from product-ops and are tagged with the customer ticket id. Creation and deletion of those snapshots are audited and visible in our operational log (we can provide a redacted audit extract). Default TTL for debug snapshots is 14 days unless extended for an active support engagement.

On attestation: we can countersign and route the attestation PDF directly to legal@brightleafhealth.com. I’ve attached the attestation and retention matrix to this thread (same files Markus sent). If you want specific contractual language, Grace and I can propose an exhibit that maps our defaults and the custom options (e.g., snapshot scrubbing).

Would you like an exec-level sign-off (VP Legal) on a countersigned attestation, or will a countersigned Privacy Ops attestation suffice for procurement?

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Privacy Operations, Redwood Inference
